lead: Spokane plumbing deals with cold winters, older South Hill homes and sprinkler systems that need winterizing. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Spokane.
risk: frozen pipes and sprinkler lines, aging pipes in older homes and basement water heaters
risk_short: frozen pipes, old pipes and water heaters
why: Browne's Addition, the South Hill and the Garland District have homes from the 1890s to the 1940s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and clay sewer laterals.
Winters freeze sprinkler systems, hose bibs and pipes near exterior walls. Many homes have basements with water heaters, floor drains and laundry.
water: Spokane pumps all of its water from wells in the Spokane Valley-Rathdrum Prairie Aquifer. It is moderately hard and needs little treatment.
problems: Frozen sprinkler lines and hose bibs
tips: Blow out sprinkler lines before the first freeze.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
areas: PipeMend works in Browne's Addition, the South Hill, Peaceful Valley, the Garland District, Hillyard, Logan and every other Spokane neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Spokane Development Services Center, and plumbers must hold a certificate from the Washington State Department of Labor and Industries.

faq.q: Where does Spokane's water come from?
faq.a: All of it comes from wells in the Spokane Valley-Rathdrum Prairie Aquifer, one of the most productive aquifers in the region. The water is moderately hard and is lightly treated.
